newsitem.title: USA: Northwest Pipe to pursue more acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Pipe to pursue more acquisitions.

text.p: Northwest Pipe Co said Tuesday it is continuing its current acquisition strategy following the recent completion of three deals.
"We are continuing to seek acquisitions that will complement and expand our business," William Tagmyer, chief executive officer, said in a statement.

Northwest Pipe, a maker of welded steel pipe, acquired Thompson Pipe & Steel in May 1996, portions of California Steel Pressure Pipe Co in December, and a tubular products mill last August. Tagmyer said the company was pleased with the progress on each deal.

The Thompson acquisition is now contributing to company earnings. The Riverside, Calif., facility was restarted in January and Northwest expects it will produce earnings in the second quarter. The tubular products mill is expected to begin production late in the third quarter.
"We believe (further) opportunities exist for continued expansion that will improve our position in our core businesses and improve our capability to respond to customer requirements," Tagmyer said.
Northwest Pipe today reported lower first quarter profits but higher sales.
Tagmyer said the company's project-oriented Water Transmission business was impacted by competitive pricing that carried over from the latter part of 1996.
He said pricing has been mixed in 1997 on relatively light bidding activity, but the company expects project bidding to increase for the balance of 1997.
